name: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos
funding: Small cultural foundation built with German, Austrian, Swiss and Dutch government grants and the City of Granada; closed by the Nicaraguan state in 2024.
watch: Founded 1987-89 by Ernesto Cardenal and Dietmar Schönherr. Ran art and music schools and Radio Volcán.
records_note: The foundation's archive site names its 2022 board but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list; closed in 2024.

overview: Cultural centre in the Casa de los Leones (House of the Lions) in Granada, a house dated to 1720 and named for the two stone lions at its portal (Casa de los Tres Mundos, La Verdad Nica).

Founded in 1987 by the Austrian actor Dietmar Schönherr and the Nicaraguan poet Ernesto Cardenal, who acquired the building from the heirs of Julio Cardenal to restore it as an international cultural centre (Casa de los Tres Mundos).

The house had been rebuilt by Julio Cardenal Argüello in 1924 with a neoclassical facade and a second floor, and served as a residence, shop, factory, toy workshop and private primary school until 1987 (Casa de los Tres Mundos).

The main building and first two patios were restored by 1992 using traditional methods, the auditorium was finished in 1994 and the old Granada courthouse was added and restored (Casa de los Tres Mundos).

Programmes listed on its archive site: a music school, the Infantilarte art school, an artists' studio, a graphic studio, a school of scenic arts, LoCreo, local development in Malacatoya, Música en los Barrios, Radio Volcán, a municipal archive and an art library (Casa de los Tres Mundos).

The government of Nicaragua closed the foundation in August 2024, including Radio Volcán, which employed about 20 workers. The house had been operating with the radio station and a group of painters who kept an exhibition space and an art school (La Verdad Nica, Augusto Cermeño, 27 August 2024).
details.funding_verdict: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos: funded by the governments of Germany, Austria, Switzerland and the Netherlands and by the City of Granada
funding: The foundation's history page names its funders as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the German federal government (for monument conservation), the federal government of Austria (North-South Institute), the Swiss government (COSUDE), the Dutch government (News Project) and the City of Granada (stated by the space).
wider_context: Confidencial (Redacción Confidencial, 12 February 2026) reports that on 19 August 2024 the Nicaraguan Executive outlawed the foundation along with 1,499 other nonprofit associations "for alleged noncompliance with the law", and ordered the movable and immovable assets of those organisations transferred to the State of Nicaragua. It reports that the building was seized by the State in August 2024.

La Verdad Nica (Augusto Cermeño, 27 August 2024) reported that the government closed the foundation, including Radio Volcán, and that the government had begun removing NGOs from circulation about three years earlier.

Confidencial reports that on 11 February 2026 a presidential decree declared the seized building National Cultural Heritage, and that Granada City Hall sources said an event centre with a restaurant would open there.
The foundation is one of the organisations outlawed on 19 August 2024; its funders named on its own history page are foreign governments and the City of Granada.
details.bottom_line: The foundation's named funders are the governments of Germany, Austria, Switzerland and the Netherlands and the City of Granada, according to its own history page. The Nicaraguan government outlawed it on 19 August 2024 along with 1,499 other organisations and took the building, which a presidential decree declared National Cultural Heritage in February 2026.

name: Hamhung Grand Theatre
funding: State theatre built in 1984, the largest in North Korea, used for major productions by a revolutionary opera troupe.
watch: A Russian opera troupe staged Eugene Onegin here in 2010, Koryo Tours says. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State theatre built in 1984, the largest in North Korea, used for major productions by a revolutionary opera troupe.
affiliations_note: Venue of a revolutionary opera troupe and of local bands, per Koryo Tours and Wikipedia.

overview: Theatre in Hamhung, which Koryo Tours calls North Korea's second-largest city, fronted by a square that Koryo Tours says is used for leisure and for rehearsing mass events.
Built in 1984, it is the largest theatre in North Korea (Koryo Tours; Wikipedia).
Koryo Tours describes a brutalist concrete exterior that towers over the square.
Koryo Tours says the entrance hall has grey marble, spiral staircases and a large mural, the auditorium seats some thousands, and dozens of rooms serve for practice and training.

Wikipedia says the revolutionary opera troupe uses it for major productions. Koryo Tours adds performances by local bands, including the Samjiyon Band, and says a visiting Russian opera troupe staged Eugene Onegin there in 2010.
Koryo Tours says anyone passing through the city can visit the exterior, and that the interior can be entered only on rare occasions when a performance is on.
details.funding_verdict: Hamhung Grand Theatre (Hamhung): state-run: a state theatre
funding: The state announces its budget only as yearly percentage changes. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5% of 2025 and spending 105.8%, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1% of last year's.

red_flags.heading: Sanctions, state body
points: Executive Order 13722 of 15 March 2016 blocks property of the Government of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea that is in the United States or in the control of US persons (Federal Register, 18 March 2016). The theatre is a state body, and the order does not name it.

details.bottom_line: The theatre is paid for by the North Korean state. The Sanctions basis is the weak point: the Government of North Korea is blocked under Executive Order 13722. Worth watching: visits by foreign troupes, such as the Russian opera troupe in 2010.

name: Korean Central History Museum
funding: Collection of about 100,000 relics; its 19 halls show over 4,000 objects (Koryo Tours). The museum claimed 10 million cumulative visitors by 2015. Kim Il Sung founded it in 1945.
why_flagged: Collection of about 100,000 relics; its 19 halls show over 4,000 objects (Koryo Tours). The museum claimed 10 million cumulative visitors by 2015. Kim Il Sung founded it in 1945.

propaganda.summary: Founded by Kim Il Sung on 1 December 1945 and housed on Kim Il Sung Square since 1977. Exhibits run from the Stone Age to 1919 with political teaching on struggle against invaders and revolution.

overview: National history museum at the north end of Kim Il Sung Square, Pyongyang, in one of the neoclassical buildings round the square (Wikipedia, Koryo Tours).
Established on 1 December 1945 by Kim Il Sung, originally on Moran Hill. Koryo Tours says it opened in the Moranbong district in 1945 (Wikipedia, Koryo Tours).

Wikipedia says the first building was destroyed in the Korean War, which it attributes to US troops, and the museum was rebuilt on the square in 1960, with 1977 given as an alternative date. Koryo Tours says it moved there in 1977.

Wikipedia counts 19 rooms, 10,500 square metres and about 100,000 relics. Koryo Tours says "over 10,000 m2" in 19 halls, as an official figure, and over 4,000 objects. The two sources do not agree on the number of objects.

Displays run from the Old Stone Age to the March First Uprising of 1919, including a mock-up of the Tomb of Tangun and the "Lolang Basket" (Koryo Tours). Koryo Tours says politicised lessons on the struggle against invaders, oppression and revolution are woven in, and calls the evidence for Tangun "supposed".

Wikipedia says that in 2014 Kim Jong Un wanted it to serve as a base standard for history museums, and that the museum claimed 10 million visitors since 1945 by 2015. Both claims come from state-linked media.
Visiting: open to foreign tourists. Photography inside is prohibited. A small shop sells ceramics and celadon (Koryo Tours, 21 October 2020).
details.funding_verdict: Korean Central History Museum: owner and funder not named in any page opened
funding: Wikipedia names Kim Il Sung as founder and cites state media.
details.bottom_line: The weak points are the lack of any published budget or governance and the museum's reliance on state media for its figures. Worth watching: any independent count of its collection and visitors.

name: Korean Folklore Museum
funding: State museum of Korean folk customs, opened February 1956 beside the Central History Museum. A 2014 reference book counts 7 rooms and 2,100 exhibits.
watch: A state description mirrored on korea-dpr.com counts over 2,300 items in 7 halls. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State museum of Korean folk customs, opened February 1956 beside the Central History Museum. A 2014 reference book counts 7 rooms and 2,100 exhibits.
records_note: It is a state institution, and North Korea reports its state budget only as yearly percentage changes (spending up 3.8 percent in 2025, per the Korea Institute for National Unification).

overview: State museum of Korean folk customs in the Central District of Pyongyang, north of the Korean Central History Museum and next to the Taedong Gate (Wikipedia, Korean Wikipedia).
Opened in February 1956 (Wikipedia, korea-dpr.com).
Wikipedia, citing a 2014 reference book, counts seven rooms of 1,800 square metres with 2,100 exhibits.
korea-dpr.com, the Korean Friendship Association's site, describes 7 halls with over 2,300 items from the Old Stone Age to the end of the 19th century.
details.funding_verdict: Korean Folklore Museum: state-funded: the Government of North Korea
funding: North Korea announces its state budget as yearly percentage changes, not amounts. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5 percent of 2025 and spending 105.8 percent, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1 percent of last year's and 15.8 percent of spending going to national defence.

red_flags.heading: Sanctions on the state
points: US Executive Order 13722 of 15 March 2016 blocks property in US jurisdiction of the Government of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea; section 9 defines the Government as the DPRK government and its agencies, instrumentalities and controlled entities (Federal Register, 18 March 2016).

details.bottom_line: The money behind the museum is the North Korean state's. The weak point is the sanctions basis under Executive Order 13722. The two item counts, 2,100 (Wikipedia) and over 2,300 (korea-dpr.com), come from different sources.

name: Mangyongdae Revolutionary Museum
funding: State museum at the site the state presents as Kim Il Sung's birthplace. Koryo Tours says it opened to the public in 1970.
watch: Koryo Tours lists it with the Native House. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State museum at the site the state presents as Kim Il Sung's birthplace. Koryo Tours says it opened to the public in 1970.
records_note: It is a state institution, and North Korea reports its state budget only as yearly percentage changes (spending up 3.8 percent in 2025, per the Korea Institute for National Unification).
affiliations_note: Part of Mangyongdae, a historic site since 1947 and a listed Revolutionary Site (Wikipedia).

propaganda.summary: Opened to the public in 1970 beside Kim Il Sung's birthplace, a state designated revolutionary site. Exhibits present his childhood and portray his family members as patriot revolutionaries.

overview: State museum at Mangyongdae on the banks of the Taedong River, a short walk from Mangyongdae Funfair (Koryo Tours).
Opened to the public in 1970 (Koryo Tours).
Lonely Planet places it near Kim Il Sung's birthplace and says it continues the theme of his childhood.
Mangyongdae has been a designated historic site since 1947 and is listed as a Revolutionary Site. Wikipedia says the original structures were replaced with replicas.
Wikipedia says state propaganda claims Mangyongdae as Kim Il Sung's birthplace while his memoirs name the nearby neighbourhood of Chilgol.
Koryo Tours lists the Native House with childhood relics, a well, a study site, a pine tree and the Sunhwa School among the sights.
Visiting: Koryo Tours asks visitors to dress respectfully, with no flip-flops, to avoid running, shouting or chewing gum, and not to step on the stone marker at the house.
details.funding_verdict: Mangyongdae Revolutionary Museum: state-funded: the Government of North Korea
funding: North Korea announces its state budget as yearly percentage changes, not amounts. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5 percent of 2025 and spending 105.8 percent, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1 percent of last year's and 15.8 percent of spending going to national defence.

points: US Executive Order 13722 of 15 March 2016 blocks property in US jurisdiction of the Government of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea; section 9 defines the Government as the DPRK government and its agencies, instrumentalities and controlled entities (Federal Register, 18 March 2016).

press.overall: Two outlets opened mention the museum or its site. A travel guide describes the museum; a defector-run outlet mentions Mangyongdae in passing.

items.title: "Mangyongdae Revolutionary Museum" (undated entry)
points: Says the museum makes the point that every member of Kim Il Sung's family was a Korean patriot and revolutionary of the humblest sort.
Describes the museum's message without criticising it.

items.title: Jang Seiul, "Kim Il Sung-Kim Jong Il Fund, 'Using the Dead to Exploit the Living'" (2024)
points: Unverified: the author, a defector, writes that all North Koreans are compelled to visit sites he calls sacred, such as Mangyongdae, through their party, youth union or labour organisations (NK Insider describes itself as analysis about North Korea by North Koreans; advocacy source).
Names Mangyongdae in one sentence; the piece is about the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, not this museum.

details.bottom_line: The money behind the museum is the North Korean state's. The weak point is the sanctions basis under Executive Order 13722. The state's birthplace claim for the site differs from what Kim Il Sung wrote in his memoirs, as Wikipedia reports.

name: North Pyongan Provincial Revolutionary History Museum
funding: State museum for North Pyongan Province, two storeys, in central Sinuiju.
watch: Photos are not allowed inside. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State museum for North Pyongan Province, two storeys, in central Sinuiju.
affiliations_note: Provincial museum of North Pyongan Province, separate from the Sinuiju History Museum in the same city.

overview: Two-storey exhibition on revolutionary activity in North Pyongan Province, in the centre of Sinuiju on the Chinese border, across from the Chinese city of Dandong (Koryo Tours).
The museum sits directly behind an open square holding the bronze monuments of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il (Koryo Tours).
Sinuiju is the capital of North Pyongan Province and the main overland port of entry for tourists and foreign trade (Koryo Tours).
Koryo Tours says the displays cover the leaders' activities and those of other figures in the region, and present Sinuiju's postwar rebuilding as part of the national story.
Koryo Tours says photos are not allowed inside.

funding: The state announces its budget only as yearly percentage changes. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5% of 2025 and spending 105.8%, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1% of last year's.

name: Party Founding Museum
funding: Museum of the Workers' Party's founding on Haebang Hill, opened October 1970. KCNA said servicepersons and working people visit it.
watch: Holds Kim Il Sung's preserved offices and meeting hall. The Government of North Korea and Workers' Party are blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: Museum of the Workers' Party's founding on Haebang Hill, opened October 1970. KCNA said servicepersons and working people visit it.
records_note: North Korea reports its state budget only as yearly percentage changes (spending up 3.8 percent in 2025, per the Korea Institute for National Unification).
affiliations_note: Includes the nearby house where Kim Il Sung lived, which Wikipedia counts as part of the museum.

propaganda.summary: Opened October 1970 in the building where Kim Il Sung proclaimed the Workers' Party of Korea on 10 October 1945. Preserves the meeting hall and plays Kim's founding speech to visitors.

overview: Museum of the founding of the Workers' Party of Korea, on the south side of Haebang Hill in the Central District of Pyongyang (Wikipedia, korea-dpr.com).

Housed in a building completed in November 1923 under Japanese rule as the South Pyongan Province commodity exhibition hall, later a department store, and after 1945 the Party's offices (Korean Wikipedia, Wikipedia).
CNN described a pre-war Japanese-style colonial building with photos and artifacts on the ground floor and the upper floor kept as in the Party's early days.
Turned into the museum in October 1970 (KCNA, Wikipedia).
KCNA claimed in 2009 that it holds two offices of Kim Il Sung, a reception room and a meeting hall arranged as they were, plus show rooms on the Party's founding.

KCNA says his residence and a monument put up for the Party's 30th anniversary stand beyond the main building. Wikipedia counts the house as part of the museum and dates an earlier monument on the museum grounds to 10 October 1975 (Wikipedia's article on the Monument to Party Founding).
details.funding_verdict: Party Founding Museum: state-funded: the Government of North Korea
funding: North Korea announces its state budget as yearly percentage changes, not amounts. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5 percent of 2025 and spending 105.8 percent, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1 percent of last year's and 15.8 percent of spending going to national defence.

red_flags.heading: Sanctions on the state and the Workers' Party
points: US Executive Order 13722 of 15 March 2016 blocks property in US jurisdiction of the Government of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea; section 9 defines the Government as the DPRK government and its agencies, instrumentalities and controlled entities (Federal Register, 18 March 2016).
The museum presents the founding of the Party the order names, in what CNN calls the Party's original headquarters.

press.overall: One piece from an outlet opened discusses the museum. It is reporting from a guided visit, not art criticism.

items.title: Tim Schwarz, "North Korea: Celebration reinforces Kim dynasty's iron grip on power" (2015)
points: Describes a visit at the Party's 70th anniversary: groups taken room by room and lectured in Party history, with what he calls an almost religious reverence from the crowds.
Notes portraits of Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin in the auditorium and no portrait of Mao Zedong.

details.bottom_line: The money behind the museum is the North Korean state's. The weak point is the sanctions basis: the order names both the Government and the Party whose founding the museum presents. Worth watching: the visits timed to the Party's October anniversary, which KCNA reported in 2009.

name: Pyongyang Circus
funding: State circus company with its own theatre, paid from the state budget. Foreign visitors pay 20 euros a ticket through their guides (Koryo Tours).
watch: Won top prizes at the Monte-Carlo and Figueres festivals in 2015 and visited Seoul in 2000, per Daily NK.
why_flagged: State circus company with its own theatre, paid from the state budget. Foreign visitors pay 20 euros a ticket through their guides (Koryo Tours).
affiliations_note: Its theatre on Kwangbok Street was built in 1989 for the World Festival of Youth and Students and renovated in 2012; a circus school stands on the grounds (Korean Wikipedia). It is one of the theatres of the April Spring Friendship Art Festival (English Wikipedia).

overview: Circus theatre on Kwangbok Street, Mangyongdae District, completed in 1989 for the 13th World Festival of Youth and Students (Korean Wikipedia).

The site covers 80,000 square metres, with 54,000 square metres of floor space and 3,500 seats. A circus school stands in the grounds, and a magic theatre of about 300 seats opened beside it in 2002 (Korean Wikipedia).
Renovation: Korean Wikipedia dates it to October 2011. English Wikipedia and Koryo Tours say 2012.
Stages for ice, water and animal acts are mechanised (Koryo Tours; Korean Wikipedia).

The Korean Art website lists a National Acrobatic Troupe set up on 10 June 1952, based in the Pyongyang Acrobatic Theatre and Magic Theatre, with a Pyongyang Acrobatics School. The site claims over 90 appearances at international circus festivals and over a hundred gold and silver prizes.

Visiting: Koryo Tours says it is open all year with regular performances. Entry is 20 euros a person, paid to local guides who arrange the tickets. Photos are allowed only before and after the show, and animals appear in some shows.
details.funding_verdict: Pyongyang Circus: state-run: the Government of North Korea, plus ticket fees from foreign visitors
funding: North Korea announces its state budget as yearly percentage changes, not amounts. KCNA claimed on 24 March 2026 that 2026 revenue would reach 100.5 percent of 2025 and spending 105.8 percent, with funds for the cultural sector at 103.1 percent of last year's and 15.8 percent of spending going to national defence.

red_flags.heading: Sanctions, state circus
points: The Korean Art website lists the troupe under performing arts creative organs and says it holds the Order of Kim Il Sung.

not_related: the People's Military Circus, a second Pyongyang circus near the War Museum. Koryo Tours says it closed and its building became a concert auditorium.

press.overall: The one piece found is a 2015 Daily NK report that describes the troupe's training and prizes without criticism.

items.title: (no byline), "Pyongyang National Circus: Breaking Down Barriers" (2015)
points: Says recruits are chosen from age nine for nine years of training, on criteria including facial symmetry, flexibility and height, then enter one of seven performance sections.
Says the troupe won the Figueres golden elephant in March 2015 and a golden clown at Monte-Carlo in January, and that it went to Seoul in 2000.
Argues that audiences can appreciate the art apart from politics. Does not criticise the institution.

details.bottom_line: The circus is state-paid, and foreign visitors add 20 euros a ticket through their guides (Koryo Tours). The foreign ticket fee is the point to watch.

overview: History museum in Sinwon-dong, an urban subdivision of Sinuiju on the Chinese border (Koryo Tours).

Shows historical remains from prehistoric times to the modern era, including antiquities excavated and collected in the province, and materials on the region's history (Koryo Tours).
Sinuiju holds the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge and the former end of the Broken Bridge, which US forces bombed in the Korean War (Koryo Tours).
Koryo Tours says photos are not allowed inside.

name: Three Revolutions Exhibition
funding: State exhibition of North Korea's economic and technical work in six halls, with a planetarium. It opened in 1946 as a non-permanent industrial and agricultural exhibition, renamed 1983.
watch: Open to foreign visitors. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State exhibition of North Korea's economic and technical work in six halls, with a planetarium. It opened in 1946 as a non-permanent industrial and agricultural exhibition, renamed 1983.
records_note: It is a state institution, and North Korea reports its state budget only as yearly percentage changes (spending up 3.8 percent in 2025, per the Korea Institute for National Unification).
affiliations_note: Runs a planetarium in its central building.

propaganda.summary: Kim Il Sung founded the exhibition in 1946. It became the Three Revolutions Exhibition in 1983 and was enlarged in 1993. It presents industrial, agricultural and scientific achievements as successes of Juche ideology.

overview: State exhibition of North Korea's economic and technical work in the Ryonmot-dong area of the Sosong District, in north Pyongyang near the Victorious Fatherland Liberation War Martyrs' Cemetery (korea-dpr.com, Koryo Tours).

Began as non-permanent exhibits in August 1946, became a permanent Industrial and Agricultural Exhibition in May 1956, took its present name in September 1983 and was enlarged in April 1993 (korea-dpr.com).
Named for the ideological, technical and cultural revolutions. Koryo Tours says every development shown is presented as a success of the state ideology, Juche.
Has six halls (Koryo Tours). Wikipedia lists electronics, heavy industry, agriculture, class education and technology among the subjects.
The central building is shaped like Saturn and holds a planetarium, and the grounds show North Korean-made vehicles outdoors (Koryo Tours, Wikipedia).
Visiting: open to foreign visitors, a short drive from the city centre (Koryo Tours).

funding: North Korea announces its state budget as yearly percentage changes, not amounts. Criticises the displays, not the exhibition's funding.
